external_context.survey: CB13_03 Dingle Bay / Great Blasket sector
interpretation_evidence: INFOMAR Dingle Bay 2013 explicitly surveyed the Great Blasket sector and reported complex/craggy seabed and chart discrepancies.
INFOMAR 2026 Blasket geoscience summary describes the archipelago as shaped by ancient volcanism, deformation and ongoing marine processes.
Published structural geology reports faulting at the northern end of Great Blasket.
Navigation references describe steep/irregular depths, reefs, awash and submerged rocks around Great Blasket.

scientific_interpretation.reason: A ~15 m relief concentrated within an ~8.3 m frozen radius plus strong roughness/curvature and strong held-out backscatter is consistent with a sharp hard rocky pinnacle. The regional geology independently predicts steep faulted/rocky seabed here. No exact indexed wreck match was found, but wreck absence is not proven because public wreck inventories are incomplete.

next_falsifier: Acquire/inspect direct high-resolution bathymetric patch, independent imagery/ROV/diver record, or an exact official wreck/nautical feature match at the frozen coordinate.
